result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-019 (profile capture as a resumable step-by-step form, consent gate, optional-field rule) at commit 42530a2, branch feature/WF02-REQ-019. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report as a substitute for re-deriving my own verdict. 1. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (unrelated to this diff). npm run build myself: both workspaces clean (Next.js compiled successfully; tsc -p tsconfig.json for apps/bot clean). 2. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432), ran `npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself (applied cleanly including 0004_fancy_zombie.sql), then ran `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` myself: 13 test files / 144 tests, all passing. NOTE: TEST-RUNNER's report (test-reports/report-2026-09-07-WF02-REQ-019.yaml, handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-04-test-runner.json) claims '26 files / 288 tests' -- exactly double the true count. I independently confirmed via `find apps/bot/src -iname '*.test.ts'` (13 files exist, matches git history at commit e804213 too -- no test files were added/removed since) and by counting `it(`/`test(` occurrences per file (sums to exactly 144). This is a factual inaccuracy in TEST-RUNNER's report, not a sign of missing coverage -- the real suite is 13 files/144 tests, genuinely green, and I confirmed this myself with real output. Filing this as its own MINOR issue below (report count discrepancy), not blocking, since the underlying tests are real and passing. 3. Independently re-verified 3 acceptance criteria end-to-end with my own fixtures, my own tg_id range (1000099901/1000099903/1000099905, distinct from TEST-RUNNER's 1000000200+ range), my own values, and my own constructed harness scripts (not reused from any existing test-spec script, deleted after use): AC1 (kill+restart resumes at next field, first answers preserved): built rv-verify-ac1-phase1.ts/phase2.ts. Discovered this sandbox's process-management tooling reaps detached/background node.exe processes across separate tool-call boundaries (confirmed empirically across 3 different launch mechanisms -- bash `&`, PowerShell Start-Process, and schtasks -- all got silently killed between my 'confirm alive' call and my 'kill' call). Worked around this by performing launch+poll-for-ready+confirm-alive-via-Get-Process+DB-read-pre-kill+Stop-Process-Force+confirm-gone+DB-read-post-kill all within one PowerShell invocation -- this still exercises a genuine separate OS process (own PID 4004, own memory, launched via Start-Process from a batch file, confirmed as a real node.exe via Get-Process) with a real forceful Stop-Process -Force termination, followed by phase 2 as a wholly separate, later `npx tsx` invocation (its own process, own empty `captured` array) reading only from Postgres. Pre-kill DB state: first_name='Riley', last_name='Quinn', company='Umbrella Corp', position/is_student/experience_level all NULL. Post-kill (same row, after confirmed-gone): identical -- all 3 answers survived the hard kill. Phase 2 dispatched 'Head Engineer' and it was accepted as the `position` answer (the only sendMessage was the isStudent prompt with the student keyboard, never a re-ask of firstName/lastName/company). Read-back after phase 2: first 3 fields byte-for-byte unchanged, position='Head Engineer' newly written. PASS. AC3 (declining consent leaves zero profiles rows): built rv-verify-ac3.ts, my own tg_id 1000099903, my own chapter fixture. Dispatched /start (never tapping Agree), /profile, and a bare text message, all while unconsented. Captured: exactly 2 sendMessage entries, both the consent prompt verbatim -- the bare text message produced no reply at all (correctly, per the derive-first discipline: the derived step is consent-needed, not profile-field, so the text listener returns without acting). Read-back: `SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE user_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE tg_id = 1000099903)` = 0; consent_pd_at NULL. PASS. AC5 (phone/email entered, error path logs neither value): built rv-verify-ac5.ts, my own phone value ('+19725550147', distinct from any value used in prior reports) already on the row, my own rejected email string ('definitely-not-an-email', distinct from prior reports' 'not-an-email'). Redirected the harness's own real stdout/stderr to files. Dispatched the malformed email; captured showed exactly the fixed profile.invalidEmailFormat catalog string, never echoing the rejected input. `grep -F` for both my phone value and my rejected email string against the real stdout and stderr capture files: zero matches in either (grep exit 1) for both strings. Read-back: email still NULL, email_skipped still false -- no write occurred. PASS. All scratch files (rv-verify-ac1-phase1.ts, rv-verify-ac1-phase2.ts, rv-verify-ac3.ts, rv-verify-ac5.ts, rv-ac1-launch.bat, rv-ac1-phase1.log, rv-ac5-stdout.log, rv-ac5-stderr.log) deleted; the schtasks entry (RVAC1Verify) deleted; `docker compose down -v` torn down the scratch Postgres; `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean before writing this handoff. 4. Confirmed AC2, AC4, AC6, AC1b, AC3b, AC-schema, AC-catalog by reading TEST-RUNNER's report's stated evidence against the actual design/spec documents and spot-checking the underlying code paths referenced (handlers/profile.ts, domain/onboarding.ts, domain/profile.ts) -- did not re-run these live myself beyond what my own AC1/AC3/AC5 runs already incidentally exercised (e.g. my AC1 run's phase 2 also exercises isStudent-prompt correctness; my AC3 run also exercises the text-listener's derive-first discipline used by AC1b). Read docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md and docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md in full myself against all 6 acceptance criteria -- every AC maps to a concrete, non-deferred design element; no 'TBD' language. 5. Migration safety and reversibility (apps/bot/drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql): read the file directly -- exactly 11 statements, matching REQ-019-schema.md §5's predicted list verbatim (6 DROP NOT NULL, 5 ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT false NOT NULL). No data-loss risk for existing profiles rows: DROP NOT NULL only widens what a column may legally hold (no existing row is rewritten or can violate a looser constraint); the 5 new boolean columns carry DEFAULT false, backfilled by Postgres in the same ALTER TABLE with no separate UPDATE pass, so every pre-existing profiles row (necessarily fully-populated already, since REQ-019 is the first requirement able to produce a partial row) ends up with all 5 new flags false -- the correct 'never explicitly skipped via this new mechanism' reading for data that predates the mechanism. Down-migration re-adds NOT NULL (fails only if a genuinely in-progress row exists at rollback time, explicitly documented as a known, non-silent limitation in REQ-019-schema.md §5.1) and drops the 5 boolean columns (a lossy but non-corrupting reversal of a resumability aid, same class already accepted for REQ-016's pending_source). No other table touched, no column renamed or dropped forward. Confirmed safe as designed. 6. Confirmed full requirement scope done: git status --porcelain clean; all 6 design-doc-listed files present (apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/onboarding.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/profile.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts modified, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts, apps/bot/drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql); grepped domain/profile.ts, domain/onboarding.ts, handlers/profile.ts for TODO/FIXME/XXX -- zero matches, nothing half-implemented. 7. Checked docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-019 entry against what actually shipped: description and all 6 acceptance_criteria match the implemented scope precisely (partial writes, optionality rule, consent gate, already-complete-skips-form, /profile view+edit+chapter-change, S11 PII rule). status is still 'pending', which is correct and expected -- DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) has not run yet; not staleness. 8. ISS-0013 (CI has no Postgres service) blocking judgment: NOT blocking this release. All of this requirement's verification (BACKEND-DEV's own checks, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER's full S1-S14 pass, TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER's Step 4, and my own Step 5 re-derivation above) has genuinely executed real code against a real Postgres instance with real, reported output -- it was run locally/by-agent rather than by an automated CI job, but it was not skipped, mocked, or asserted without evidence. ISS-0013 is correctly scoped as test-infrastructure debt: it describes a gap in this pipeline's ongoing automated regression-safety net going forward (a future change could regress DB-backed behavior without CI catching it), not a defect in REQ-019's own shipped correctness today. Blocking REQ-019 on ISS-0013 would not fix the CI gap (that requires separate infrastructure work, already filed at MAJOR severity with a concrete remediation plan) -- it would only withhold already-verified, unrelated functionality. Filed correctly as MAJOR, open, forwarded -- not fixed here, per Unblock-Everything's scope boundary (a pre-existing pipeline gap noticed but not blocking this run's own acceptance criteria).

issues.title: TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report and test-report YAML state an inflated test count ('26 files / 288 tests') exactly double the actual suite ('13 files / 144 tests')
issues.description: handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-04-test-runner.json and test-reports/report-2026-09-07-WF02-REQ-019.yaml both claim 'npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (per ISS-0014): 26 files / 288 tests passed.' I independently ran the exact same command myself against a freshly migrated scratch Postgres and got 13 files / 144 tests, all passing -- exactly half the claimed count in both dimensions. Confirmed via `find apps/bot/src -iname '*.test.ts'` (13 files, matching git history at commit e804213 -- no test files were added or removed since TEST-RUNNER's run) and by summing `it(`/`test(` occurrences per file (144). This does not indicate missing or fabricated coverage -- the real 144-test suite is genuinely green, confirmed by my own independent run with real output -- but the reported figure itself is factually wrong and should be corrected at the source so a future reader doesn't build on an inflated count.
